fields.title: 📖 When water is changed by impurity
fields.body:
🖋️ **Imām ash-Shāfiʿī** said:

> ***“If the taste, color, or smell of the water changes because of something forbidden that mixes with it, the water does not become pure again until it is drawn out or a large amount of water is poured upon it, so that the taste, color, and smell of the forbidden thing disappear. When this disappears and the water returns to the state in which Allah made it purifying, then its impurity has gone.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** In the Fiqh of Ṭahārah, mere doubt does not count, but a recognizable change. If water is changed by Najāsah in **taste**, **color**, or **smell**, it no longer counts as purifying until this change disappears.

immutable.source: 📝 ash-Shāfiʿī, al-Umm / Ikhtilāf al-Ḥadīth, Kitāb aṭ-Ṭahārah, Bāb: aṭ-Ṭahārah bi-l-Māʾ.
